blogs.title: From 16‑bit to 1.58‑bit: How BitNet b1.58 Shrinks LLMs Without Losing Accuracy
blogs.description: A walkthrough of the core innovation behind BitNet b1.58 – ternary weights {-1, 0, 1} – and why this “1.58‑bit” representation can match full‑precision LLaMA models in perplexity and downstream tasks. The post explains the quantization technique, the role of the zero weight, and the intuition that fewer bits don’t have to mean weaker models.

blogs.title: Speed, Memory, Energy: The New Scaling Law for 1‑bit Large Language Models
blogs.description: Breaks down the scaling law introduced in the paper, showing how a 13B BitNet b1.58 can be more efficient than a 3B FP16 model, and a 70B b1.58 beats a 13B FP16 model. Includes visual charts translating latency, GPU memory, and energy savings into everyday analogies (e.g., “running a marathon with half the shoes”).

blogs.title: Inside BitLinear: Re‑engineering the Transformer’s Workhorse for Integer‑Only Math
blogs.description: Delves into the architectural change from nn.Linear to BitLinear, describing how matrix multiplication becomes pure integer addition. The article covers the absmean quantization function, activation handling, and why this redesign makes hardware acceleration easier.

blogs.title: Deploying LLMs on the Edge: Why 1.58‑bit Models Are a Game‑Changer for Mobile AI
blogs.description: Translates the paper’s implications for smartphones, IoT devices, and on‑device assistants. It outlines memory footprint reductions, lower power draw, and compatibility with CPUs/NPUs, and explores realistic use cases such as offline translation or personal privacy‑preserving assistants.

blogs.title: Future Hardware for 1‑bit LLMs: From GPUs to Custom LPUs
blogs.description: Explores how the BitNet computation paradigm opens doors for new accelerator designs. The post explains what “almost no multiplication” means for chip architects, reviews existing efforts like Groq’s LPUs, and sketches possible silicon implementations optimized for ternary weights and 8‑bit activations.

blogs.title: Beyond Quantization: Training Large Language Models Directly in 1.58 Bits
blogs.description: Contrasts post‑training quantization with training from scratch using ternary weights as done in BitNet b1.58. Discusses challenges (gradient estimation, stability) and solutions presented in the paper, illustrating why training at low bit‑width can outperform quantizing a full‑precision model.
